results.content: Returning inflation to 2 percent does not return prices to 2020. It means the new, substantially higher price level continues rising at 2 percent. By July 2026 headline CPI was roughly 28 percent above its January 2020 level. The rate of increase matters enormously to the Federal Reserve; the accumulated increase is what households inherited. [...] The 2026 readings also carry a more immediate burden. The Iran conflict pushed energy prices higher and revived fears that inflation would spread again, so the latest deterioration is not simply the accumulated price-level shock echoing through sentiment.
